title: WPCRL/1014/2022 of SHATRUNJAI PUNDIR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 1014 of 2022
Shatrunjai Pundir
..................Petitioner

-Versus-State of Uttarakhand and others
.............Respondents
Present: Mr. Lalit Belwal with Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General with Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, learned
A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Date of Hearing and Order: 11.07.2022
Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court
made the following order:
1. By filing this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for
issuance of a writ of Certiorari for quashing the
impugned FIR No. 0106 of 2022 dated 28.02.2022
registered under Section 498-A, 323 &504 of the Indian
Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961 by the S.H.O., Police Station
Raipur, District - Dehradun. He has also prayed for
issuance of a writ of Mandamus to record the
statements of the petitioner through virtual mode
under Section 161 of the Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code" for brevity).
2. He has prayed for consequential relief at this stage. It is
not disputed that the petitioner is residing in Mt. Cook,
Wellington, New Zealand in pursuance of his

2
employment and he should not be served notice under
Section 41A of the Code.
3. Thus, at the stage, Mr. Lalit Belwal, learned counsel for
the petitioner confines his submissions only for
recording the statements under Section 161 of the
Code with a special resort to the first proviso of Sub-Section 3, which enables recording of his statements
through Audio-Video mode.
4. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General has no
objection to the same except stating that the
Investigating Officer has intimated him that the notice
under Section 41A of the Code could not be served
upon the petitioner as he is residing outside the
country.
5. In that view of the matter, we dispose of the writ
petition by giving liberty to the petitioner to provide the
e-mail ID or his telephone number having whatsApp
facility to the learned Deputy Advocate General, who in
turn give the same to the Investigating Officer and
notice under Section 41A of the Code shall be served to
petitioner in electronic mode and then the petitioner
shall file his reply, if so advised. He may appear before
the Investigating Officer either through virtual mode or
physically. As far as, recording of his statements under
Section 161 of the Code is concerned. The Investigating
Officer shall record his statements through virtual
mode and for that the expenses shall be borne by the
petitioner.

3
6. With such observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
7. Urgent certified copy of this order be supplied to learned
counsel for the petitioner and also a free certified copy of this
order be supplied to the learned Deputy Advocate General,
for early compliance.
 ( San j ay a Ku m ar Mish r a, J.)
 11.07.2022
A/ -
